themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a coordinated flyering or vandalism campaign emerging in Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Statistically anomalous spike with high severity classification
Aligns with public space quality concerns reflected in ongoing sidewalk condition complaints
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Walk affected blocks to document what's being posted and by whom (political, commercial, gang-related?)
Enforcement angle: How quickly does DOE respond to illegal postings; are resources stretched?

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 6.33)—indicating a sudden degradation in park usability or control over late-night activities in Central Harlem's recreational spaces.
evidence: 6 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.33)
Concurrent spike in drinking-related complaints (3 complaints last week vs. 0.2 avg, 1100% increase)
Community Board repeatedly budgets for parks maintenance upgrades, suggesting chronic resource gaps
reporting_angles: Source interviews: Residents who filed complaints; park users about safety and usability
NYC Parks response: Are staffing levels adequate; what's the enforcement posture on evening/night hours?
Connection to homelessness: Do unsheltered populations congregating in parks correlate with noise spikes?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints surged to 18 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 4.9 per week—a 269% increase (z-score: 6.91)—suggesting accelerating street-level infrastructure decay across Central Harlem.
evidence: 18 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 4.9 weekly average (269% spike, z-score: 6.91)
Concurrent spike in litter basket requests (5 last week vs. 0.4 avg, 1233% increase, z-score: 9.55)
DOE has filed 458 building permits in past 90 days; ongoing ULURP projects may be disrupting sidewalk conditions
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Document sidewalk conditions in affected neighborhoods; photograph hazards
DOE and NYCTA accountability: Are construction projects leaving sidewalks unsafe; what's the repair timeline?
Community impact: Interview elderly and disabled residents about accessibility risks

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints rose to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 471% increase (z-score: 5.28)—coinciding with recent violent crime reports and suggesting emerging public safety concerns in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (471% spike, z-score: 5.28)
Gothamist reported gunman custody/manhunt in Harlem on 2026-04-25 (concurrent timeframe)
Concurrent spikes in drinking complaints (1100%) and park noise (700%) suggest broader disorder
reporting_angles: NYPD enforcement: Interview precinct command on patrol strategy and resource allocation in response to spike
Resident safety perception: Conduct interviews in neighborhoods with highest complaint density
Root cause analysis: Are supply routes shifting; is addiction treatment capacity adequate?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crisis (Lagging Signal)
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked 3 weeks ago to 7 complaints from a baseline of 0.8 per week—an 833% increase (z-score: 5.74)—though the spike is aging, it may reflect ongoing street vending enforcement gaps or unauthorized street commerce.
evidence: 7 vendor enforcement complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% spike, z-score: 5.74)
THE CITY reported on Mamdani's Municipal Grocery challenges on 2026-04-23 (same timeframe), suggesting commercial/vendor tensions
Spike is cooling but may indicate systemic gaps in vendor licensing or sidewalk permit enforcement
reporting_angles: Follow-up on THE CITY grocery story: Is vendor enforcement being weaponized against small businesses?
DOE vendor enforcement: Interview about staffing, complaint backlog, and equitable enforcement practices
